edition.headline: Shares memory across coding agents, constrains browser model output, orchestrates agents and more
edition.dek: The strongest items today are tooling that makes agents and small models easier to run: shared agent memory, schema-bound output in the browser, and an open orchestrator from Google. events.title: vshulcz/deja-vu
events.summary: One memory shared by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, OpenClaw and 28 more coding agents, built from the session history already on disk. brief.headline: deja-vu shares one memory across coding agents
brief.newly_possible: You can search and reuse fixes from past sessions across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI and others, using history already on disk.
brief.why: It needs no LLM or embeddings, only one local Go binary, so it is cheap to add to existing setups.

Reduces repeated debugging across different agents

hats.architect: Memory lives locally and is built from existing history, so no new service is needed.
hats.security: Session history may hold secrets, so check what it indexes.
hats.data: Works on months of existing sessions without re-processing through a model.
hats.scout: Supports 33 agents in total per the repo description.
hats.combinator: Cross-agent memory could be a wedge for a team-level product.
